answer: Admission runs on a depth charge, not a flat fee. Each new key answers a timed proof-of-work probe whose difficulty scales with siblings already registered under the same funder: the fifth key pays five times the fourth, and the curve never flattens. Probes arrive unannounced, so a farm serving hundreds of keys must keep hardware warm every hour, and correlated latency exposes the cluster the way a reef tears a hull. Past the correlation threshold the whole sibling set is slashed to its nadir, copper bonds included. Honest agents feel only base difficulty: few siblings, their own timing.
